findings.description: The security group allows TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploitation attempts against the instance.

The user_data script embeds a static AWS access key ID and secret access key. User data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by any process or SSRF on the host, and the secret is also stored in plaintext in Terraform state and VCS.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data written to the attached disk is stored unencrypted and any snapshot or underlying storage exposure yields cleartext data.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains available and an SSRF against the web server can steal instance role credentials. The root block device also lacks encryption.
The bucket receiving VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, so sensitive network telemetry is stored unencrypted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL, or bucket policy restrictions are defined, leaving the flow-log bucket vulnerable to accidental public exposure of network traffic records.
force_destroy = true with no versioning means audit/flow-log data can be irrecoverably deleted, undermining forensic integrity of security logs.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume, so the backup data is also stored unencrypted and could be exposed if snapshot permissions are misconfigured.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet to receive a public IP, placing workloads directly on the internet alongside the wide-open security group.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically exposes instances in this subnet to the internet via public IPs, increasing attack surface.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting a compromised instance to exfiltrate data or reach command-and-control infrastructure without restriction.
